column1: # Lotus tools for the AI – one list for every AI in Lotus: the /ai terminal, and later the web chat and the pets.
# The AI only sees the tools of features that are on; it cannot invent or call others.
# feature  the Lotus feature it belongs to (data/features.tsv) – off means the tool is not offered
# level    read: runs right away · act: asks first (allowed in auto mode or when the user allows Lotus features)
# mode     run: Lotus runs it and hands the result back · tty: it gets the terminal until the user closes it
# command  the lotus command, one word per space; {name} is a parameter, [{name}] an optional one
# params   name:type:required:description; … – types: text, int(min,max), enum(a|b|c), path
#          enum(@themes) and enum(@features) are filled in from Lotus' own lists

column8: What Lotus has here: version, theme, language, which features are on and off, keep-awake. Use it before saying a feature is missing.

column7: app:text:1:The app's name – typos are fine
column8: Open an installed Mac app by its name. When several apps could be meant, it lists them instead of guessing.

column7: query:text:1:What to look for, e.g. "browser" or "Firefox"
column8: Search Lotus' app catalog (and Homebrew) for apps to install, with what each one is and whether it is installed.

column7: app:text:1:The exact name from find_app, or a Homebrew cask
column8: Install a Mac app with Homebrew. The user approves it first. Use find_app first when you are not sure of the exact name.

column7: place:text:0:A city; leave it out for the user's own city
column8: The weather now and the forecast for the next days.
What is playing right now in Spotify, Music or another player.
Play, pause, skip, go back or change the volume of what is playing.
Change the color theme of Lotus (the start screen, the AI terminal, the clock).

column7: design:enum(minimal|big|retro|matrix|analog|world):0:The design – leave it out for the user's favorite
column8: Open the full-screen clock in this terminal. The user closes it with q, then the conversation goes on.

column7: minutes:int(0,1440):1:How long in minutes; 0 keeps it awake until it is turned off
column8: Keep the Mac awake for a while with macOS' caffeinate, e.g. during a download, a render or a server.
Turn a Lotus feature on or off. A feature that is off has no commands and downloads nothing.
The Minecraft servers set up with Lotus, and whether they are running.

column7: server:text:1:The server's folder name from minecraft_servers
column8: Start a Minecraft server set up with Lotus, in its own Terminal window.
Remove the background of an image on this Mac. Lotus shows its progress and saves a new PNG next to it; the original stays.
